record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: Given a Ramsey Euclidean set X and an integer r, how can one determine or bound N(X,r), the least dimension threshold such that every r-coloring of Euclidean N-space for all sufficiently large N contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X, even in the basic case where X has two points?

evidence.quote: Recall that given a Ramsey set X and an integer r, we defined N (X, r) to be the least integer such that if N > N (X, r) then for any r-coloring of EN , there is a monochromatic X 0 ∈ Cong(X). One might go farther than asking which sets are Ramsey; given a Ramsey set and an integer r, what can we say about N (X, r)? As we’ll see below, even for the simplest nontrivial case, a 2-point set, this is a major open question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a finite set X ⊂ ℝ^d a Ramsey set if for every positive integer r there exists an integer N such that for every N' ≥ N, every coloring of ℝ^{N'} with r colors contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X (i.e. an isometric image of X all of whose points receive the same color). For such a Ramsey set X and a positive integer r, define

  N(X, r) := the least integer N₀ such that for every N > N₀ and every r-coloring of ℝ^N, there is a monochromatic congruent copy of X.

Problem: For Ramsey sets X and integers r ≥ 2, determine or give good upper and lower bounds for N(X, r). In particular, treat the basic case in which X = {p, q} consists of two points at some fixed distance: determine the asymptotic behavior of N({p,q}, r) as a function of r (equivalently, determine how large the dimension N must be to guarantee that every r-coloring of ℝ^N contains two points at the prescribed distance receiving the same color).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers in Euclidean Ramsey theory (including work by Conlon–Fox on lines and 2025 surveys on the subject) continue to describe the determination of N(X,r), and even the 2-point case (closely related to the chromatic number of ℝ^N), as a major open problem with only exponential-type bounds known.

status_evidence.title: Lines in Euclidean Ramsey theory (Conlon–Fox)
status_evidence.snippet: There exist red/blue-colorings of E^n containing no red copy of ℓ_2 and no blue copy of ℓ_m for any m ≥ 2^(cn), best possible up to the constant c.
status_evidence.claim: Best known bounds for N(X,r) in the 2-point/line case are exponential, with the precise dependence still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Biggest Open Problem in Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Patel, REU 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Euclidean Ramsey theory framed around still-open questions including dimension thresholds for Ramsey sets.
status_evidence.claim: The determination of N(X,r) remains a central open problem, even for very simple X.
